SaaS Unit Economics Report

Calculated from the dbt_to_exports tables

Published

October 30, 2026

This report reads the nine tables that the dbt_to_exports model writes to csv_exports/. The exports only count and add up. All the rates, ratios and growth figures below are calculated here.

The report stops at 2025-12. The exports run to 2028-12, but nothing after 2025 is loaded, so no 2026, 2027 or 2028 figure can reach a chart or table.

Where an export also carries a ready-made rate (e.g., arpu, retention_rate), the notebook recalculates it from the underlying counts and dollars and compares the two. The comparison is in the data checks section.

When saas_dashboard_data.xlsx (the old dashboard’s workbook) sits next to this file, the data checks also compare every chart’s numbers with it.

Export table One row per Used for
monthly_metrics_long calendar month and metric MRR, customer counts
mrr_movements_long calendar month and movement type New, expansion, contraction, churn
nrr_long calendar month and segment NRR by plan tier and channel
cohort_metrics_long cohort, month of life, segment, metric Retention and cohort revenue
cac_per_customer_by_channel cohort and channel Acquisition cost
unit_economics_by_cohort cohort, channel, plan tier 24-month LTV and CAC
arr_by_month, arr_movements_long, kpi_summary month Cross-checks only

Setup

Show code 
# Shorthand used in variable names (business terms like MRR, ARR, CAC, LTV, NRR, ARPU, KPI are kept as is)
#   coh = cohort        mvmts = movements     mo = month         pct = percent
#   custs = customers   seg = segment         chan = channel     unit_econ = unit economics
#   xl = the old dashboard's Excel workbook   chk = check        rebuilt = recalculated here from the exports
#   cum = cumulative    ser = series          tbl = table        win = one of the three tab windows

import pandas as pd, numpy as np
from pathlib import Path

    """Display a table with a clean index."""
    display(df.reset_index(drop=kw.pop("drop", True)).style.hide(axis="index").format(precision=2, thousands=","))

def dt(idx):
    """'2022-01' strings to dates."""
    return pd.to_datetime(pd.Index(idx).astype(str) + "-01")

def yearaxis(ax):
    ax.xaxis.set_major_locator(mdates.YearLocator())
    ax.xaxis.set_major_formatter(mdates.DateFormatter("%Y"))

def endlabel(ax, x, y, text, color):
    ax.annotate(text, (x, y), xytext=(6, 0), textcoords="offset points", color=color,
                va="center", fontsize=9, fontweight="bold", annotation_clip=False)

def dollars(unit="", dec=0):
    return mt.FuncFormatter(lambda v, _: f"${v:,.{dec}f}{unit}")

Load the exports

Show code 
tbls = {path.stem: pd.read_csv(path) for path in sorted(EXPORT_DIR.glob("*.csv"))}

# Nothing after the cutoff is allowed into the report
CUTOFF = "2025-12"
LAST_FULL_COHORT = str(pd.Period(CUTOFF, "M") - 23)   # '2024-01': its 24th month is 2025-12

# The three two-year tabs, as (first month, last month). Used by the old-dashboard check and by every chart below
WINDOWS = {"2022-2023": ("2022-01", "2023-12"),
           "2023-2024": ("2023-01", "2024-12"),
           "2024-2025": ("2024-01", "2025-12")}

for tbl_name, date_col in [("monthly_metrics_long", "calendar_month"), ("mrr_movements_long", "calendar_month"),
                  ("nrr_long", "calendar_month"), ("arr_by_month", "calendar_month"),
                  ("arr_movements_long", "calendar_month"), ("kpi_summary", "period"),
                  ("cac_per_customer_by_channel", "cohort_month")]:
    tbls[tbl_name] = tbls[tbl_name][tbls[tbl_name][date_col].astype(str) <= CUTOFF]

# Cohort rows are cut by the calendar month they land in (cohort month + months of life)
coh_long_raw = tbls["cohort_metrics_long"]
coh_ordinal = {cohort: pd.Period(cohort, "M").ordinal for cohort in coh_long_raw.cohort_month.unique()}
tbls["cohort_metrics_long"] = coh_long_raw[coh_long_raw.cohort_month.map(coh_ordinal) + coh_long_raw.period <= pd.Period(CUTOFF, "M").ordinal]

# 24-month LTV only exists for cohorts whose 24th month is on or before the cutoff
tbls["unit_economics_by_cohort"] = tbls["unit_economics_by_cohort"].query("cohort_month <= @LAST_FULL_COHORT")

# Month-level tables, one column per metric
mo_metrics = (tbls["monthly_metrics_long"].query("segment_type == 'all'")
      .pivot(index="calendar_month", columns="metric_name", values="metric_value"))
mrr_mvmts = (tbls["mrr_movements_long"]
      .pivot(index="calendar_month", columns="movement_type", values="delta_value").fillna(0))

# Cohort table for all customers, one column per metric
coh_metrics = (tbls["cohort_metrics_long"].query("segment_type == 'all'")
       .pivot_table(index=["cohort_month", "period"], columns="metric_name", values="metric_value"))

inventory = pd.DataFrame({
    "table": list(tbls),
    "rows": [len(tbl) for tbl in tbls.values()],
    "columns": [", ".join(tbl.columns) for tbl in tbls.values()]})
inventory["columns"] = inventory["columns"].str.slice(0, 200)
show(inventory)

Data checks

Each check compares two tables, or an export column against the same number rebuilt here. The status line below tells us whether to trust what follows. The detail is in section 8.

Show code 
CHECKS = []

def check(name, rebuilt, exported, tol=1e-6):
    """Max absolute gap between a rebuilt number and the exported one."""
    rebuilt_al, exported_al = pd.Series(rebuilt).align(pd.Series(exported), join="inner")
    gap = (rebuilt_al - exported_al).abs().replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).max()
    CHECKS.append({"check": name, "rows_compared": int(rebuilt_al.notna().sum()),
                   "largest_gap": gap, "passed": bool(gap <= tol)})

prior_mrr = mo_metrics.total_mrr.shift(1)
prior_active = mo_metrics.active_customers.shift(1)

check("ARPU = MRR / active customers", mo_metrics.total_mrr / mo_metrics.active_customers, mo_metrics.arpu)
check("Logo churn % = churned / prior active", mo_metrics.churned_customers / prior_active * 100, mo_metrics.logo_churn_rate_pct)
check("Revenue churn % = churn dollars / prior MRR", -mrr_mvmts.Churn / prior_mrr * 100, mo_metrics.revenue_churn_rate_pct)
check("Active customers roll forward", prior_active + mo_metrics.new_customers - mo_metrics.churned_customers, mo_metrics.active_customers)
check("Movements add up to the MRR change", mrr_mvmts.sum(axis=1), mo_metrics.total_mrr.diff().fillna(mo_metrics.total_mrr), tol=1e-4)

arr_tbl = tbls["arr_by_month"].set_index("calendar_month")
check("ARR = 12 x MRR", 12 * mo_metrics.total_mrr, arr_tbl.arr_value, tol=1e-4)
check("ARR table MRR matches monthly MRR", mo_metrics.total_mrr, arr_tbl.total_mrr)
arr_mvmts = tbls["arr_movements_long"].pivot(index="calendar_month", columns="movement_type", values="delta_value").fillna(0)
check("ARR movements = 12 x MRR movements", (arr_mvmts - 12 * mrr_mvmts).abs().max(axis=1), pd.Series(0.0, index=mrr_mvmts.index), tol=1e-4)

nrr_all = tbls["nrr_long"].query("segment_type == 'all'").set_index("calendar_month").nrr_percentage.sort_index()
check("NRR = (prior MRR + expansion + contraction + churn) / prior MRR",
      (prior_mrr + mrr_mvmts.Expansion + mrr_mvmts.Contraction + mrr_mvmts.Churn) / prior_mrr * 100, nrr_all)

# kpi_summary against the monthly table
kpi_cmp = tbls["kpi_summary"].merge(
    tbls["monthly_metrics_long"].rename(columns={"calendar_month": "period", "metric_value": "monthly_value"}),
    on=["segment_type", "segment_value", "metric_name", "period"], how="left")
check("KPI current value = monthly value", kpi_cmp.current_value, kpi_cmp.monthly_value)
kpi_cmp = kpi_cmp.sort_values(["metric_name", "period"])
check("KPI previous value = last month's value", kpi_cmp.groupby("metric_name").current_value.shift(1), kpi_cmp.previous_value)
check("KPI % change = (current - previous) / previous",
      (kpi_cmp.current_value - kpi_cmp.previous_value) / kpi_cmp.previous_value * 100, kpi_cmp["pct_change"], tol=1e-6)

# Cohort table
coh_size = coh_metrics.active_customers.groupby(level="cohort_month").transform("first")
coh_start_mrr = coh_metrics.mrr_total.groupby(level="cohort_month").transform("first")
check("Retention % = active / starting customers", coh_metrics.active_customers / coh_size * 100, coh_metrics.retention_rate)
check("MRR retention % = MRR / starting MRR", coh_metrics.mrr_total / coh_start_mrr * 100, coh_metrics.mrr_retention_rate)
check("Avg MRR = cohort MRR / starting customers", coh_metrics.mrr_total / coh_size, coh_metrics.avg_mrr)
ltv_rebuilt = coh_metrics.avg_mrr.groupby(level="cohort_month").cumsum()
check("Cumulative LTV = running sum of avg MRR", ltv_rebuilt, coh_metrics.cumulative_ltv)

coh_rows = coh_metrics.reset_index()
coh_rows["calendar_month"] = (pd.PeriodIndex(coh_rows.cohort_month, freq="M") + coh_rows.period).astype(str)
by_cal_mo = coh_rows.groupby("calendar_month")[["active_customers", "mrr_total"]].sum()
check("Cohorts add up to monthly active customers", by_cal_mo.active_customers, mo_metrics.active_customers)
check("Cohorts add up to monthly MRR", by_cal_mo.mrr_total, mo_metrics.total_mrr, tol=1e-4)
check("Period 0 customers = new customers", coh_metrics.xs(0, level="period").active_customers.rename_axis("calendar_month"), mo_metrics.new_customers)

# Segments add up to all customers
seg_p0 = tbls["cohort_metrics_long"].query("metric_name == 'active_customers' and period == 0")
coh_start_custs = seg_p0.query("segment_type == 'all'").set_index("cohort_month").metric_value
for seg_type in ["channel", "plan_tier"]:
    check(f"{seg_type} segments add up to all customers (period 0)",
          seg_p0.query("segment_type == @seg_type").groupby("cohort_month").metric_value.sum(), coh_start_custs)

unit_econ = tbls["unit_economics_by_cohort"]
check("Mature customers by cohort <= cohort size", (unit_econ.groupby("cohort_month").mature_customers.sum() - coh_start_custs).clip(lower=0), pd.Series(0.0, index=coh_start_custs.index))


# Compare with the old dashboard's workbook, when it sits next to the report
XL_PATH = Path("saas_dashboard_data.xlsx")
XL_NOTE = ""
if XL_PATH.exists():
    xl_sheets = pd.read_excel(XL_PATH, sheet_name=None)
    def xl_vals(sheet, keys, val):
        """One value per key. The three tabs overlap, and overlapping months repeat the same numbers."""
        return xl_sheets[sheet].drop_duplicates(subset=keys).set_index(keys)[val]
    def chk_vs_xl(label, sheet, keys, val, rebuilt, tol=0.006):
        check(f"Old dashboard, {label}", rebuilt, xl_vals(sheet, keys, val), tol=tol)
    mo_key = ["calendar_month"]
    chk_vs_xl("total MRR", "total_mrr", mo_key, "mrr", mo_metrics.total_mrr)
    chk_vs_xl("ARR run-rate", "arr", mo_key, "arr_run_rate", 12 * mo_metrics.total_mrr, tol=0.02)
    for mvmt_name in ["New Business", "Expansion", "Contraction", "Churn"]:
        chk_vs_xl(f"MRR movement, {mvmt_name}", "mrr_movements", mo_key, mvmt_name, mrr_mvmts[mvmt_name])
    chk_vs_xl("net MRR growth", "mrr_movements", mo_key, "Net MRR Growth", mrr_mvmts[["New Business", "Expansion", "Contraction", "Churn"]].sum(axis=1))
    chk_vs_xl("ARPU", "arpu", mo_key, "arpu", mo_metrics.total_mrr / mo_metrics.active_customers, tol=1e-3)
    chk_vs_xl("revenue churn %", "revenue_churn", mo_key, "revenue_churn_rate_pct", -mrr_mvmts.Churn / prior_mrr * 100, tol=1e-3)
    for col, rebuilt_ser in [("active_customers", mo_metrics.active_customers), ("new_customers", mo_metrics.new_customers), ("churned_customers", mo_metrics.churned_customers)]:
        chk_vs_xl(f"customers, {col}", "customer_counts", mo_key, col, rebuilt_ser, tol=1e-9)
    chk_vs_xl("logo churn %", "customer_churn", mo_key, "churn_rate_percentage", mo_metrics.churned_customers / prior_active * 100, tol=1e-3)
    chk_vs_xl("NRR, all customers", "nrr_all", mo_key, "nrr_percentage", nrr_all, tol=1e-3)
    for sheet, seg_type, col in [("nrr_by_channel", "channel", "channel"), ("nrr_by_plan_tier", "plan_tier", "plan_tier")]:
        rebuilt_ser = tbls["nrr_long"].query("segment_type == @seg_type").rename(columns={"segment_value": col}).set_index([col, "calendar_month"]).nrr_percentage
        chk_vs_xl(f"NRR by {seg_type}", sheet, [col, "calendar_month"], "nrr_percentage", rebuilt_ser, tol=1e-3)
    cac_chan_chk = tbls["cac_per_customer_by_channel"].pivot(index="cohort_month", columns="channel", values="cohort_cac")
    chan_custs_chk = seg_p0.query("segment_type == 'channel'").pivot(index="cohort_month", columns="segment_value", values="metric_value")
    blend_cac_chk = (cac_chan_chk * chan_custs_chk).sum(axis=1) / chan_custs_chk.sum(axis=1)
    chk_vs_xl("CAC by channel", "cac_by_channel", ["channel", "cohort_month"], "cac_per_customer_dollars",
           cac_chan_chk.stack().rename_axis(["cohort_month", "channel"]).swaplevel().sort_index(), tol=1e-3)
    chk_vs_xl("blended CAC", "cac_blended", ["cohort_month"], "blended_cac_dollars", blend_cac_chk, tol=1e-3)

    def xl_heat_long(sheet, keys):
        sheet_df = xl_sheets[sheet].drop_duplicates(subset=keys)
        month_cols = [cohort for cohort in sheet_df.columns if str(cohort).isdigit()]
        stacked = sheet_df.set_index(keys)[month_cols].rename(columns=int).stack()
        stacked.index.names = keys + ["period"]
        return stacked
    coh_long_chk = tbls["cohort_metrics_long"]
    def heat_rebuilt(metric, seg_type=None):
        metric_rows = coh_long_chk[coh_long_chk.metric_name == metric]
        if seg_type is None:
            return metric_rows.query("segment_type == 'all'").set_index(["cohort_month", "period"]).metric_value
        return metric_rows.query("segment_type == @seg_type").rename(columns={"segment_value": seg_type}).set_index([seg_type, "cohort_month", "period"]).metric_value
    check("Old dashboard, customer retention heatmap", heat_rebuilt("retention_rate"), xl_heat_long("cohort_retention_heatmap", ["cohort_month"]), tol=1e-3)
    check("Old dashboard, revenue retention heatmap", heat_rebuilt("mrr_retention_rate"), xl_heat_long("revenue_retention_heatmap", ["cohort_month"]), tol=1e-3)
    check("Old dashboard, retention by channel", heat_rebuilt("retention_rate", "channel"), xl_heat_long("retention_by_channel", ["channel", "cohort_month"]), tol=1e-3)
    check("Old dashboard, retention by plan tier", heat_rebuilt("retention_rate", "plan_tier"), xl_heat_long("retention_by_plan_tier", ["plan_tier", "cohort_month"]), tol=1e-3)

    # 24-month LTV and CAC by channel and plan tier, per tab
    ue_rows = []
    for timeframe, (win_start, win_end) in WINDOWS.items():
        win_unit_econ = unit_econ[unit_econ.cohort_month.between(win_start, win_end)]
        seg_totals = win_unit_econ.assign(ltv_tot=win_unit_econ.ltv_24m * win_unit_econ.mature_customers, cac_tot=win_unit_econ.average_cac * win_unit_econ.mature_customers).groupby(["channel", "plan_tier"])[["mature_customers", "ltv_tot", "cac_tot"]].sum()
        seg_totals["ltv_24m"], seg_totals["average_cac"], seg_totals["ratio"] = (seg_totals.ltv_tot / seg_totals.mature_customers,
                                                                        seg_totals.cac_tot / seg_totals.mature_customers,
                                                                        seg_totals.ltv_tot / seg_totals.cac_tot)
        seg_totals["timeframe"] = timeframe; ue_rows.append(seg_totals.reset_index().set_index(["timeframe", "channel", "plan_tier"]))
    unit_econ_rebuilt = pd.concat(ue_rows)
    for xl_col, rebuilt_col in [("mature_customers", "mature_customers"), ("ltv_24m", "ltv_24m"), ("average_cac", "average_cac"), ("ltv_to_cac_ratio", "ratio")]:
        check(f"Old dashboard, unit economics {xl_col}", unit_econ_rebuilt[rebuilt_col], xl_sheets["unit_economics_table"].set_index(["timeframe", "channel", "plan_tier"])[xl_col], tol=1e-3)

    # Payback month: the workbook counts whole months after the signup month
    def payback_xl(cohort):
        cum_ltv = np.r_[0.0, coh_metrics.loc[cohort].cumulative_ltv.dropna().values]; hit = np.where(cum_ltv >= blend_cac_chk[cohort])[0]
        return np.floor((hit[0] - 1) + (blend_cac_chk[cohort] - cum_ltv[hit[0] - 1]) / (cum_ltv[hit[0]] - cum_ltv[hit[0] - 1])) if len(hit) else np.nan
    check("Old dashboard, payback month", pd.Series({cohort: payback_xl(cohort) for cohort in blend_cac_chk.index}),
          xl_vals("ltv_cac_payback", ["cohort_month"], "payback_lifetime_month"), tol=1e-9)
else:
    XL_NOTE = " The old dashboard's workbook was not found next to this file, so that comparison was skipped."

checks = pd.DataFrame(CHECKS)
n_ok = int(checks.passed.sum())
status = "All" if n_ok == len(checks) else f"Only {n_ok} of"
display(Markdown(f"**Data checks.** {status} {len(checks)} checks passed." + XL_NOTE))

Windows and status rules

Each chart has three tabs. A tab is a two-year window. The table and the colored badge on that tab compare the window’s last month with the month before it and with the same month a year earlier.

Show code 
# WINDOWS (the three tab date ranges) is defined in the load section above.

def win_bounds(name):
    """start, end, prior month, year-ago month for a tab."""
    start, end = WINDOWS[name]
    end_period = pd.Period(end, "M")
    return start, end, str(end_period - 1), str(end_period - 12)

# Latest month in the report (pages 2 and 3 still use these)
last_mo, prior_mo, yago_mo = mo_metrics.index[-1], mo_metrics.index[-2], mo_metrics.index[-13]

def windowaxis(ax, start, end, months=(1, 4, 7, 10)):
    ax.set_xlim(pd.Timestamp(start + "-01") - pd.Timedelta(days=15), pd.Timestamp(end + "-01") + pd.Timedelta(days=15))
    ax.xaxis.set_major_locator(mdates.MonthLocator(bymonth=list(months)))
    ax.xaxis.set_major_formatter(mdates.DateFormatter("%b %Y"))

# Every metric the badges and status tables can use: (series, display kind, how change is shown)
# "pct" = percent change (dollars and counts).  "pts" = difference in percentage points (rates).
mrr_growth_pct = mo_metrics.total_mrr.pct_change() * 100
logo_churn_pct = mo_metrics.churned_customers / mo_metrics.active_customers.shift(1) * 100
rev_churn_pct = -mrr_mvmts.Churn / mo_metrics.total_mrr.shift(1) * 100
METRICS = {
    "MRR ($)": (mo_metrics.total_mrr, "$", "pct"),
    "ARR ($)": (12 * mo_metrics.total_mrr, "$", "pct"),
    "Active customers": (mo_metrics.active_customers, "n", "pct"),
    "ARPU ($)": (mo_metrics.total_mrr / mo_metrics.active_customers, "$", "pct"),
    "New customers": (mo_metrics.new_customers, "n", "pct"),
    "Churned customers": (mo_metrics.churned_customers, "n", "pct"),
    "Net new MRR ($)": (mrr_mvmts.sum(axis=1), "$", "pct"),
    "Logo churn (% of last month)": (logo_churn_pct, "%", "pts"),
    "Revenue churn (% of last month)": (rev_churn_pct, "%", "pts"),
    "Net revenue retention (%)": (pd.Series(nrr_all), "%", "pts"),
    "MRR growth vs previous month (%)": (mrr_growth_pct, "%", "pts"),
}

# (which direction is good, "flat" below this size, "watch" below this size, otherwise "bad")
# These cut-offs are judgment calls. Edit them here and every badge and table follows.
RULES = {
    "MRR ($)": ("up", 0.5, 2.0),            # percent change
    "ARR ($)": ("up", 0.5, 2.0),
    "Active customers": ("up", 0.5, 2.0),
    "ARPU ($)": ("up", 0.5, 2.0),
    "New customers": ("up", 2.0, 10.0),
    "Churned customers": (None, 0, 0),      # grows with the base, so the rates judge it
    "Net new MRR ($)": ("up", 2.0, 10.0),
    "Logo churn (% of last month)": ("down", 0.10, 0.50),   # points
    "Revenue churn (% of last month)": ("down", 0.10, 0.50),
    "Net revenue retention (%)": ("up", 0.25, 1.00),
    "MRR growth vs previous month (%)": (None, 0, 0),   # falls on its own as the base grows, so MRR dollars carry the verdict
}

def judge_raw(now, then, how, better, flat, watch):
    """Return (change, status). Status is Good, Watch, Bad, Flat or Context."""
    if pd.isna(now) or pd.isna(then) or (how == "pct" and then == 0):
        return np.nan, "n/a"
    ch = (now / then - 1) * 100 if how == "pct" else now - then
    if better is None:
        return ch, "Context"
    if abs(ch) < flat:
        return ch, "Flat"
    if (ch > 0) == (better == "up"):
        return ch, "Good"
    return ch, "Watch" if abs(ch) < watch else "Bad"

def judge(label, now, then):
    better, flat, watch = RULES[label]
    return judge_raw(now, then, METRICS[label][2], better, flat, watch)

def fmt(v, kind):
    if pd.isna(v): return "n/a"
    return f"${v:,.0f}" if kind == "$" and abs(v) > 1000 else f"${v:,.2f}" if kind == "$" else f"{v:,.0f}" if kind == "n" else f"{v:.2f}%"

def fmt_change(ch, how):
    if pd.isna(ch): return "n/a"
    return f"{ch:+.1f}%" if how == "pct" else f"{ch:+.2f} pts"

def arrow(ch):
    return "" if pd.isna(ch) else "▲" if ch > 0 else "▼" if ch < 0 else "▬"

STATUS_CSS = {"Good": "background-color:#e6f4ec;color:#1a7f4b;font-weight:600",
              "Watch": "background-color:#fff3d6;color:#9a5b00;font-weight:600",
              "Bad": "background-color:#fde8e6;color:#b42318;font-weight:600",
              "Flat": "background-color:#eeeeee;color:#555555",
              "Context": "background-color:#eeeeee;color:#555555",
              "Above average": "background-color:#e6f4ec;color:#1a7f4b;font-weight:600",
              "Average": "background-color:#eeeeee;color:#555555",
              "Below average": "background-color:#fff3d6;color:#9a5b00;font-weight:600",
              "Baseline": "background-color:#eeeeee;color:#555555",
              "n/a": ""}

def chip(label, e, ref, caption):
    """Badge that sits above a chart, at its top right. Arrow = direction. Color = good or bad."""
    s, kind, how = METRICS[label]
    ch, st = judge(label, s[e], s[ref])
    display(HTML(
        f'<div class="kpi-row"><div class="kpi-chip kpi-{st.lower().replace("/", "")}">'
        f'<span class="kpi-label">{label}<br>{caption}</span>'
        f'<span class="kpi-val">{arrow(ch)} {fmt_change(ch, how)}</span>'
        f'<span class="kpi-tag">{st}</span></div></div>'))

def status_table(e, p, y, labels):
    """Latest value, change vs prior month and vs year ago. The two verdict columns come last."""
    rows, css = [], []
    for lab in labels:
        s_, kind, how = METRICS[lab]
        row = {"Metric": lab, f"Latest ({e})": fmt(s_[e], kind)}
        sty = {"Metric": "", f"Latest ({e})": ""}
        verdicts = {}
        for ref, c_chg, c_tag in [(p, "vs prior month", "Verdict (month)"), (y, "vs year ago", "Verdict (year)")]:
            ch, st = judge(lab, s_[e], s_[ref])
            row[c_chg] = f"{arrow(ch)} {fmt_change(ch, how)}".strip(); sty[c_chg] = STATUS_CSS[st]
            verdicts[c_tag] = st
        for c_tag, st in verdicts.items():
            row[c_tag] = st; sty[c_tag] = STATUS_CSS[st]
        rows.append(row); css.append(sty)
    df, cs = pd.DataFrame(rows), pd.DataFrame(css)
    return df.style.hide(axis="index").apply(lambda _: cs, axis=None)
Show code 
def badge(label, caption, text, status):
    """Same badge as chip(), for values that are not a month-over-month change."""
    display(HTML(
        f'<div class="kpi-row"><div class="kpi-chip kpi-{status.lower()}">'
        f'<span class="kpi-label">{label}<br>{caption}</span>'
        f'<span class="kpi-val">{text}</span><span class="kpi-tag">{status}</span></div></div>'))

# How each metric is summarised over a year in the year-over-year tables
BASIS = {"MRR ($)": "Dec", "ARR ($)": "Dec", "Active customers": "Dec", "ARPU ($)": "Dec",
         "New customers": "Total", "Churned customers": "Total", "Net new MRR ($)": "Total",
         "Logo churn (% of last month)": "Avg", "Revenue churn (% of last month)": "Avg",
         "Net revenue retention (%)": "Avg", "MRR growth vs previous month (%)": "Avg"}
BASIS_TXT = {"Dec": "December value", "Total": "Full-year total", "Avg": "Average month"}

def year_value(lab, yr):
    x = METRICS[lab][0]; x = x[x.index.str[:4] == yr]
    b = BASIS[lab]
    return x.iloc[-1] if b == "Dec" else x.sum() if b == "Total" else x.mean()

def yoy_table(name, labels):
    """First year of the tab against the second year, with a Good/Bad verdict."""
    s, e, p, y = win_bounds(name); y1, y2 = s[:4], e[:4]
    display(Markdown(f"**Year over year, {y1} vs {y2}.**"))
    rows, css = [], []
    for lab in labels:
        kind, how = METRICS[lab][1], METRICS[lab][2]
        v1, v2 = year_value(lab, y1), year_value(lab, y2)
        ch, st = judge(lab, v2, v1)
        rows.append({"Metric": lab, "Basis": BASIS_TXT[BASIS[lab]], y1: fmt(v1, kind), y2: fmt(v2, kind),
                     "Change": f"{arrow(ch)} {fmt_change(ch, how)}".strip(), "Verdict": st})
        css.append({"Metric": "", "Basis": "", y1: "", y2: "", "Change": STATUS_CSS[st], "Verdict": STATUS_CSS[st]})
    cs = pd.DataFrame(css)
    display(pd.DataFrame(rows).style.hide(axis="index").apply(lambda _: cs, axis=None))

1 Headline numbers

Each tab is a two-year window. The table compares the window’s last month with the month before it and with the same month a year earlier. The arrow shows which way the number moved. The color shows whether that move is good for the business. A lower churn rate shows ▼ in green. The second table sets the first year of the tab against the second. Churned customers get no verdict because their count grows with the customer base. The churn rates judge them instead.

2 Revenue growth

Monthly recurring revenue (MRR) is the subscription revenue we bill each month. Annual recurring revenue (ARR) is 12 times that. The top chart shows the level. The bottom chart shows growth versus the previous month, so each point compares that month’s MRR with the month before it. The first month of the report has nothing before it, so the growth line starts in February 2022.

The tables compare the window’s last month with the month before and with the same month a year earlier. Growth in percent falls on its own as the base gets bigger, so it carries no verdict. MRR, ARR and ARPU carry the verdict.

Show code 
GROWTH_LABELS = ["MRR ($)", "ARR ($)", "ARPU ($)", "MRR growth vs previous month (%)"]

def sec_growth(name):
    s, e, p, y = win_bounds(name)
    chip("MRR ($)", e, p, f"{e} vs {p}")
    m = mo_metrics.total_mrr.loc[s:e]
    unit, div, dec_ = ("M", 1e6, 1) if m.max() >= 1.5e6 else ("K", 1e3, 0)
    gg = mrr_growth_pct.loc[s:e].dropna()
    fig, (a1, a2) = plt.subplots(2, 1, figsize=(9, 6), sharex=True, height_ratios=[2.2, 1])
    a1.plot(dt(m.index), m / div, color=BLUE, lw=2.4)
    a1.set_ylim(bottom=0); a1.set_ylabel(f"MRR ($ {'millions' if unit == 'M' else 'thousands'})")
    a1.yaxis.set_major_formatter(dollars(unit, dec_)); a1.set_title("Monthly recurring revenue")
    a2.plot(dt(gg.index), gg.values, color=INK, lw=1.8)
    a2.set_ylim(bottom=0); a2.set_ylabel("Growth (%)"); a2.set_title("Growth vs. previous month")
    windowaxis(a2, s, e); fig.tight_layout(); plt.show()
    below = gg[gg < 5]
    tail = (f"It first dropped below 5% in **{below.index[0]}**. " if len(below) else f"It stayed above 5% through {e}. ")
    display(Markdown(
        f"Growth vs. the previous month was **{gg.iloc[0]:.1f}%** in {gg.index[0]} and **{gg[e]:.1f}%** in {e}. " + tail +
        "A smaller percentage on a much bigger base still adds more dollars, which is why MRR keeps climbing."))
    display(status_table(e, p, y, GROWTH_LABELS))
    yoy_table(name, GROWTH_LABELS)

3 MRR movements

Every month, MRR changes for four reasons. New business adds revenue. Expansion adds more from existing customers. Contraction and churn take revenue away. The black line is the net result.

The table gives each movement in dollars and as a share of the prior month’s MRR. The verdict judges the dollars against the month before. For churn and contraction a smaller loss is good. The share column has no verdict, because shares shrink on their own as MRR grows.

Show code 
MOVES = ["New Business", "Expansion", "Contraction", "Churn"]
# (good direction, "flat" below this % change, "watch" below this % change), applied to the dollar amount
MOVE_RULES = {"New Business": ("up", 2.0, 10.0), "Expansion": ("up", 2.0, 10.0), "Net new MRR": ("up", 2.0, 10.0),
              "Contraction": ("down", 2.0, 10.0), "Churn": ("down", 2.0, 10.0)}

def movement_table(e, p):
    rows, css = [], []
    for mname in MOVES + ["Net new MRR"]:
        ser = mrr_mvmts[MOVES].sum(axis=1) if mname == "Net new MRR" else mrr_mvmts[mname]
        now, then = ser[e], ser[p]
        if mname in ("Contraction", "Churn"):
            now, then = abs(now), abs(then)           # a loss that grows is bad
        ch, st = judge_raw(now, then, "pct", *MOVE_RULES[mname])
        rows.append({"Movement": mname, "Dollars": f"${ser[e]:,.0f}", "% of prior-month MRR": f"{ser[e] / mo_metrics.total_mrr[p] * 100:+.2f}%",
                     "Dollars vs prior month": f"{arrow(ch)} {fmt_change(ch, 'pct')}", "Verdict": st})
        css.append({"Movement": "", "Dollars": "", "% of prior-month MRR": "",
                    "Dollars vs prior month": STATUS_CSS[st], "Verdict": STATUS_CSS[st]})
    return pd.DataFrame(rows).style.hide(axis="index").apply(lambda _: pd.DataFrame(css), axis=None)

def sec_movements(name):
    s, e, p, y = win_bounds(name)
    chip("Net new MRR ($)", e, p, f"{e} vs {p}")
    k = mrr_mvmts.loc[s:e] / 1e3; d = dt(k.index)
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(9.5, 5))
    ax.bar(d, k["New Business"], width=25, color=MOVE["New Business"], label="New Business")
    ax.bar(d, k["Expansion"], width=25, bottom=k["New Business"], color=MOVE["Expansion"], label="Expansion")
    ax.bar(d, k["Churn"], width=25, color=MOVE["Churn"], label="Churn")
    ax.bar(d, k["Contraction"], width=25, bottom=k["Churn"], color=MOVE["Contraction"], label="Contraction")
    ax.plot(d, k[MOVES].sum(axis=1), color=INK, lw=1.8, label="Net new MRR")
    ax.axhline(0, color="#888888", lw=0.8)
    ax.yaxis.set_major_formatter(dollars("K")); ax.set_ylabel("Change in MRR ($ thousands)")
    ax.set_title("What changed MRR each month"); ax.legend(ncol=5, loc="upper left")
    windowaxis(ax, s, e); plt.show()
    m = mrr_mvmts.loc[e]
    display(Markdown(f"Movements in **{e}**, compared with {p}."))
    display(movement_table(e, p))
    display(Markdown(
        f"New business added **${m['New Business']:,.0f}** and expansion added **${m.Expansion:,.0f}**. "
        f"{'Expansion' if m.Expansion > m['New Business'] else 'New business'} was the bigger source of growth. "
        f"Churn and contraction together removed **${-(m.Churn + m.Contraction):,.0f}**. "
        f"Expansion alone covered **{m.Expansion / -(m.Churn + m.Contraction) * 100:.0f}%** of the losses."))

def sec_customers(name):
    s, e, p, y = win_bounds(name)
    chip("Active customers", e, p, f"{e} vs {p}")
    m = mo_metrics.loc[s:e]; d = dt(m.index)
    fig, (a1, a2) = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(10.5, 3.9))
    a1.plot(d, m.active_customers, color=BLUE, lw=2.2)
    a1.set_ylim(bottom=0); a1.set_title("Active customers")
    a1.yaxis.set_major_formatter(mt.FuncFormatter(lambda v, _: f"{v:,.0f}"))
    a1.annotate(f"{m.active_customers.iloc[-1]:,.0f}", (d[-1], m.active_customers.iloc[-1]),
                xytext=(-4, 6), textcoords="offset points", ha="right", fontsize=9)
    a2.plot(d, m.new_customers, color=BLUE, lw=1.8, label="New")
    a2.plot(d, m.churned_customers, color=ORANGE, lw=1.8, label="Churned")
    a2.set_ylim(bottom=0); a2.set_title("New and churned customers per month"); a2.legend(loc="upper left")
    for a in (a1, a2): windowaxis(a, s, e, months=(1, 7))
    fig.tight_layout(); plt.show()
    peak = m.new_customers.idxmax()
    display(Markdown(
        f"We ended {e} with **{m.active_customers[e]:,.0f}** active customers. "
        f"The last month added **{m.new_customers[e]:,.0f}** and lost **{m.churned_customers[e]:,.0f}**. "
        f"New sign-ups peaked at **{m.new_customers.max():,.0f}** in {peak}."))
    display(status_table(e, p, y, ["Active customers", "New customers", "Churned customers"]))
    yoy_table(name, ["Active customers", "New customers", "Churned customers"])

Churn rates tell us how fast customers and dollars leave, relative to the size of the base. Logo churn counts customers. Revenue churn counts dollars. A lower rate is better, so a falling line is good news.

Show code 
def sec_churn(name):
    s, e, p, y = win_bounds(name)
    chip("Logo churn (% of last month)", e, p, f"{e} vs {p}")
    lc, rc = logo_churn_pct.loc[s:e].dropna(), rev_churn_pct.loc[s:e].dropna()
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(9, 4.4))
    ax.plot(dt(lc.index), lc.values, color=BLUE, lw=2, label="Logo churn")
    ax.plot(dt(rc.index), rc.values, color=ORANGE, lw=2, label="Revenue churn")
    ax.set_ylim(bottom=0); ax.set_ylabel("% of last month"); ax.set_title("Monthly churn rates")
    ax.legend(loc="upper right"); windowaxis(ax, s, e); plt.show()
    f = lc.index[0]
    display(Markdown(
        f"Logo churn {'fell' if lc[e] < lc[f] else 'rose'} from **{lc[f]:.1f}%** in {f} to **{lc[e]:.2f}%** in {e}. "
        f"Revenue churn is {'lower' if rc[e] < lc[e] else 'higher'} at **{rc[e]:.2f}%**. "
        + ("The customers who leave pay less than the average customer, so each loss costs less than its share of revenue."
           if rc[e] < lc[e] else "The customers who leave pay more than the average customer.")))
    display(status_table(e, p, y, ["Logo churn (% of last month)", "Revenue churn (% of last month)"]))
    yoy_table(name, ["Logo churn (% of last month)", "Revenue churn (% of last month)"])

5 Net revenue retention

Net revenue retention (NRR) asks one question. If we had no new customers, would revenue go up or down? Above 100% means the customers we already have are paying more in total than a month ago. Each tab draws every month of its window. The badge tracks NRR for all customers. The numbers match the old dashboard’s workbook, and the data checks prove it.

Show code 
nrr_long = tbls["nrr_long"]
# The export rows are in shuffled order, so every series is sorted by month before it is sliced
nrr_series = {(st, sv): g_.set_index("calendar_month").nrr_percentage.sort_index()
         for (st, sv), g_ in nrr_long.groupby(["segment_type", "segment_value"])}
NRR_ORDER = [("all", "all")] + [("plan_tier", q) for q in SEGMENT_ORDER["plan_tier"]] + [("channel", c) for c in SEGMENT_ORDER["channel"]]

def sec_nrr(name):
    s, e, p, y = win_bounds(name)
    chip("Net revenue retention (%)", e, p, f"{e} vs {p}")
    fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(11, 4.4), sharey=True)
    for ax, st, pal, ttl in [(axes[0], "plan_tier", TIER, "By plan tier"), (axes[1], "channel", CHAN, "By channel")]:
        for nm in SEGMENT_ORDER[st]:
            x = nrr_series[(st, nm)].loc[s:e].dropna()
            ax.plot(dt(x.index), x.values, color=pal[nm], lw=1.7, label=nm)
        ax.axhline(100, color="#666666", lw=0.9, ls="--")
        ax.set_title(ttl); windowaxis(ax, s, e, months=(1, 7))
        ax.legend(loc="upper center", bbox_to_anchor=(0.5, -0.1), ncol=3)
    axes[0].set_ylabel("NRR (%)"); fig.tight_layout(); plt.show()
    y1, y2 = s[:4], e[:4]
    rows, css = [], []
    for k in NRR_ORDER:
        x = nrr_series[k]; a1_, a2_ = x[x.index.str[:4] == y1].mean(), x[x.index.str[:4] == y2].mean()
        c1, s1 = judge_raw(x[e], x[p], "pts", *RULES["Net revenue retention (%)"])
        c2, s2 = judge_raw(a2_, a1_, "pts", *RULES["Net revenue retention (%)"])
        rows.append({"Group": "All customers" if k[0] == "all" else k[1].title(),
                     "Cut by": "" if k[0] == "all" else k[0].replace("_", " "),
                     f"NRR {e} (%)": f"{x[e]:.2f}", "vs prior month": f"{arrow(c1)} {fmt_change(c1, 'pts')}",
                     f"Avg {y1} (%)": f"{a1_:.2f}", f"Avg {y2} (%)": f"{a2_:.2f}", "Avg change": f"{arrow(c2)} {fmt_change(c2, 'pts')}",
                     "Verdict (month)": s1, "Verdict (year)": s2})
        css.append({c: "" for c in rows[-1]} | {"vs prior month": STATUS_CSS[s1], "Verdict (month)": STATUS_CSS[s1],
                                               "Avg change": STATUS_CSS[s2], "Verdict (year)": STATUS_CSS[s2]})
    cs = pd.DataFrame(css)
    display(pd.DataFrame(rows).style.hide(axis="index").apply(lambda _: cs, axis=None))
    below = [k[1] for k in NRR_ORDER if k[0] != "all" and nrr_series[k][e] < 100]
    display(Markdown(
        f"Every group is at or above 100% in {e}." if not below else
        f"Groups below 100% in {e} are **{', '.join(below)}**. Their existing customers shrank in total."))

6 Cohort retention

A cohort is everyone who signed up in the same month. Each tab shows the cohorts that signed up in that two-year window, followed through 2025-12 and no further. Each row of a heatmap is one cohort. Each column is the number of months since signup. Darker blue means more customers are still active.

The badge compares month-6 retention for cohorts that signed up in the first year of the tab with the second year. Higher is better.

Show code 
coh_long = tbls["cohort_metrics_long"]
active_by_seg = (coh_long.query("metric_name == 'active_customers'")
       .pivot_table(index=["segment_type", "segment_value", "cohort_month"], columns="period", values="metric_value"))
all_cohorts = sorted(coh_metrics.index.get_level_values("cohort_month").unique())

def cohorts_in(name):
    s, e, _, _ = win_bounds(name)
    return [c for c in all_cohorts if s <= c <= e]

def ret_at(st, sv, month, cohorts):
    """Share of starting customers still active at `month`, using cohorts old enough to have reached it."""
    P = active_by_seg.loc[(st, sv)]; P = P.loc[P.index.isin(cohorts)]
    if month not in P.columns: return np.nan
    now = P[month].dropna()
    return now.sum() / P.loc[now.index, 0].sum() * 100 if len(now) else np.nan

def rev_ret(month, cohorts):
    r = coh_metrics.reset_index(); r = r[r.cohort_month.isin(cohorts)]
    now = r[r.period == month].set_index("cohort_month").mrr_total
    start = r[r.period == 0].set_index("cohort_month").mrr_total.reindex(now.index)
    return now.sum() / start.sum() * 100 if len(now) else np.nan

def yr_cohorts(name):
    s, e, _, _ = win_bounds(name); cs = cohorts_in(name)
    return [c for c in cs if c[:4] == s[:4]], [c for c in cs if c[:4] == e[:4]]

def cohort_chip(label, name, fn, how="pts", better="up", flat=0.5, watch=2.0):
    """Badge: first-year cohorts of the tab against second-year cohorts."""
    c1, c2 = yr_cohorts(name); a, b = fn(c1), fn(c2)
    ch, st = judge_raw(b, a, how, better, flat, watch)
    badge(label, f"{name[5:]} vs {name[:4]} cohorts", f"{arrow(ch)} {fmt_change(ch, how)}", st)

def cohort_table(name, label, fn, months=(1, 6, 12, 24), how="pts", rule=(0.5, 2.0)):
    """First-year cohorts of the tab against second-year cohorts, month by month. Verdict last."""
    c1, c2 = yr_cohorts(name); y1, y2 = name[:4], name[5:]
    f = lambda v: "n/a" if pd.isna(v) else f"{v:.1f}%"
    rows, css = [], []
    for m in months:
        a_, b_ = fn(m, c1), fn(m, c2)
        ch, st = judge_raw(b_, a_, how, "up", *rule)
        rows.append({"Month of life": f"Month {m}", f"{y1} cohorts": f(a_), f"{y2} cohorts": f(b_),
                     "Change": "n/a" if pd.isna(ch) else f"{arrow(ch)} {fmt_change(ch, how)}", "Verdict": st})
        css.append({k: "" for k in rows[-1]} | {"Change": STATUS_CSS[st], "Verdict": STATUS_CSS[st]})
    display(Markdown(f"**{label}.** Cohorts that signed up in {y1} against cohorts that signed up in {y2}. n/a means those cohorts are not yet that old by 2025-12."))
    display(pd.DataFrame(rows).style.hide(axis="index").apply(lambda _: pd.DataFrame(css), axis=None))

def channel_table(name):
    c1, c2 = yr_cohorts(name); y1, y2 = name[:4], name[5:]
    ref = next(m for m in (12, 6, 1) if not pd.isna(ret_at("all", "all", m, c1)) and not pd.isna(ret_at("all", "all", m, c2)))
    rows, css = [], []
    for ch in SEGMENT_ORDER["channel"]:
        a_, b_ = ret_at("channel", ch, ref, c1), ret_at("channel", ch, ref, c2)
        chg, st = judge_raw(b_, a_, "pts", "up", 0.5, 2.0)
        rows.append({"Channel": ch, f"{y1} cohorts": f"{a_:.1f}%", f"{y2} cohorts": f"{b_:.1f}%",
                     "Change": f"{arrow(chg)} {fmt_change(chg, 'pts')}", "Verdict": st})
        css.append({k: "" for k in rows[-1]} | {"Change": STATUS_CSS[st], "Verdict": STATUS_CSS[st]})
    display(Markdown(f"**Month-{ref} retention by channel.** Cohorts that signed up in {y1} against cohorts that signed up in {y2}."))
    display(pd.DataFrame(rows).style.hide(axis="index").apply(lambda _: pd.DataFrame(css), axis=None))

def sec_cohort_heat(name):
    cs = cohorts_in(name)
    cohort_chip("Month-6 customer retention", name, lambda c: ret_at("all", "all", 6, c))
    M = coh_metrics.reset_index().query("cohort_month in @cs").pivot(index="cohort_month", columns="period", values="retention_rate")
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(9, 6.5))
    sns.heatmap(M, ax=ax, cmap="Blues", vmin=0, vmax=100, xticklabels=6, yticklabels=3,
                cbar_kws={"label": "Customers still active (%)", "shrink": 0.85})
    ax.grid(False); ax.set_xlabel("Months since signup"); ax.set_ylabel("Cohort (signup month)")
    ax.set_title("Customer retention by cohort"); plt.xticks(rotation=0); plt.yticks(rotation=0); plt.show()
    cohort_table(name, "Customer retention", lambda m, c: ret_at("all", "all", m, c))

The curves below average every cohort in the tab for each plan tier and channel. This split shows which channel and plan tier contributes most to retention. This will guide spending and plan tier focus for next year. The curves slope down because customers leave over time. The heatmaps above show that most customers stay, so a line that flattens high is the goal. The verdict column compares each group with all customers.

Show code 
def curve_for(st, nm, cohorts, upto=36):
    P = active_by_seg.loc[(st, nm)]; P = P.loc[P.index.isin(cohorts)]
    seen = P.notna().values
    out = P.fillna(0).values.sum(axis=0) / (P[0].values[:, None] * seen).sum(axis=0) * 100
    return pd.Series(out, index=P.columns).loc[:upto]

def sec_curves(name):
    cs = cohorts_in(name)
    fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(11, 4.4), sharey=True)
    for ax, st, pal, ttl in [(axes[0], "plan_tier", TIER, "By plan tier"), (axes[1], "channel", CHAN, "By channel")]:
        for nm in SEGMENT_ORDER[st]:
            c_ = curve_for(st, nm, cs)
            ax.plot(c_.index, c_.values, color=pal[nm], lw=2)
            endlabel(ax, c_.index[-1], c_.values[-1], nm, pal[nm])
        ax.set_title(ttl); ax.set_ylim(0, 102); ax.set_xlabel("Months since signup")
    axes[0].set_ylabel("Customers still active (%)"); fig.tight_layout(); plt.show()
    MONTHS = [1, 6, 12, 24, 36]
    groups = [("all", "all", "All customers")] + [("plan_tier", q, q) for q in SEGMENT_ORDER["plan_tier"]] \
             + [("channel", c, c) for c in SEGMENT_ORDER["channel"]]
    ref = 12 if not pd.isna(ret_at("all", "all", 12, cs)) else 6
    base = ret_at("all", "all", ref, cs)
    def vs_base(v):
        return "n/a" if pd.isna(v) else "Above average" if v - base >= 2 else "Below average" if v - base <= -2 else "Average"
    vcol = f"Verdict (month {ref})"
    rows = []
    for t, v, lab in groups:
        r = {"Group": lab, **{f"Month {m}": ("n/a" if pd.isna(ret_at(t, v, m, cs)) else f"{ret_at(t, v, m, cs):.1f}%") for m in MONTHS}}
        r[vcol] = "Baseline" if t == "all" else vs_base(ret_at(t, v, ref, cs)); rows.append(r)
    tbl = pd.DataFrame(rows)
    sty = pd.DataFrame({c: ([STATUS_CSS[x] for x in tbl[c]] if c == vcol else [""] * len(tbl)) for c in tbl.columns})
    display(Markdown(f"Share of starting customers still active, for the {len(cs)} cohorts that signed up in {name}. "
                     "Each figure uses only the cohorts old enough to have reached that month. n/a means none have yet. "
                     f"The verdict compares each group with all customers at month {ref}. Within 2 points counts as average."))
    display(tbl.style.hide(axis="index").apply(lambda _: sty, axis=None))
    cand = [g for g in groups[1:] if not pd.isna(ret_at(g[0], g[1], ref, cs))]
    best = max(cand, key=lambda g: ret_at(g[0], g[1], ref, cs)); worst = min(cand, key=lambda g: ret_at(g[0], g[1], ref, cs))
    display(Markdown(
        f"After {ref} months, **{best[2]}** keeps **{ret_at(best[0], best[1], ref, cs):.1f}%** of customers. "
        f"**{worst[2]}** keeps **{ret_at(worst[0], worst[1], ref, cs):.1f}%**."))

6.1 Revenue retention by cohort

Customer counts miss what each customer pays. This heatmap follows cohort revenue instead. Blue means the cohort pays more than in its first month. Red means it pays less. The scale runs from 0% (red) through 100% (white) to 200% (blue). The badge compares month-6 revenue retention for first-year cohorts with second-year cohorts.

    cs = cohorts_in(name)
    cohort_chip("Month-6 revenue retention", name, lambda c: rev_ret(6, c), flat=1.0, watch=3.0)
    Mr = coh_metrics.reset_index().query("cohort_month in @cs").pivot(index="cohort_month", columns="period", values="mrr_retention_rate")

7 Unit economics

Customer acquisition cost (CAC) is what we spend to win one customer. Lifetime value (LTV) here is the revenue one customer brings in during the first 24 months. LTV:CAC compares the two. A common rule of thumb asks for at least 3 to 1.

Each tab groups customers by the window they signed up in. A cohort only counts for LTV once its 24th month is on or before 2025-12, so the last tab has few of them. The tab says how many it uses.

7.1 Cost to win a customer

The export gives CAC by cohort and channel. The blended line weights each channel by the customers it brought in that month. Higher CAC is worse, so a rising cost shows ▲ in red. The badge compares blended CAC for first-year cohorts with second-year cohorts. The table compares the first 12 cohorts of the tab with the last 12.

Show code 
cac_by_chan = tbls["cac_per_customer_by_channel"].pivot(index="cohort_month", columns="channel", values="cohort_cac")[SEGMENT_ORDER["channel"]]
chan_starts = (coh_long.query("segment_type == 'channel' and metric_name == 'active_customers' and period == 0")
          .pivot(index="cohort_month", columns="segment_value", values="metric_value")[SEGMENT_ORDER["channel"]])
cac_by_chan["Blended"] = (cac_by_chan * chan_starts).sum(axis=1) / chan_starts.sum(axis=1)
CAC_RULE = ("down", 2.0, 10.0)   # percent change

def blend_cac_for(cs):
    return (cac_by_chan.loc[cs, SEGMENT_ORDER["channel"]] * chan_starts.loc[cs]).sum().sum() / chan_starts.loc[cs].sum().sum()

def sec_cac(name):
    s, e, _, _ = win_bounds(name)
    cohort_chip("Blended CAC", name, blend_cac_for, how="pct", better=CAC_RULE[0], flat=CAC_RULE[1], watch=CAC_RULE[2])
    c = cac_by_chan.loc[s:e]; d = dt(c.index)
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(9, 4.6))
    for ch in SEGMENT_ORDER["channel"]:
        ax.plot(d, c[ch], color=CHAN[ch], lw=1.8, label=ch)
    ax.plot(d, c.Blended, color=INK, lw=1.6, ls="--", label="Blended")
    ax.yaxis.set_major_formatter(dollars()); ax.set_ylabel("CAC ($)")
    ax.set_title("CAC per customer, by signup cohort"); ax.legend(ncol=4, loc="upper left"); windowaxis(ax, s, e); plt.show()
    f12, l12 = c.head(12).mean(), c.tail(12).mean()
    rows, css = [], []
    for ch in c.columns:
        chg, st = judge_raw(l12[ch], f12[ch], "pct", *CAC_RULE)
        rows.append({"Channel": ch, "First 12 cohorts ($)": f"{f12[ch]:,.2f}", "Last 12 cohorts ($)": f"{l12[ch]:,.2f}",
                     "Change": f"{arrow(chg)} {fmt_change(chg, 'pct')}", "Verdict": st})
        css.append({"Channel": "", "First 12 cohorts ($)": "", "Last 12 cohorts ($)": "", "Change": STATUS_CSS[st], "Verdict": STATUS_CSS[st]})
    cs_ = pd.DataFrame(css)
    display(pd.DataFrame(rows).style.hide(axis="index").apply(lambda _: cs_, axis=None))
    ch_only = l12.drop("Blended")
    display(Markdown(
        f"Blended CAC went from **${f12.Blended:,.0f}** to **${l12.Blended:,.0f}**. "
        f"**{ch_only.idxmax()}** is the most expensive channel at **${ch_only.max():,.0f}** a customer. "
        f"**{ch_only.idxmin()}** is the cheapest at **${ch_only.min():,.0f}**."))

7.2 LTV to CAC and payback

The table weights each cohort by the customers old enough to have a full 24 months. Each cell shows the ratio and a verdict. At or above 3 is Good, from 2 to 3 is Watch, and below 2 is Bad. The thresholds are in RATIO_RULE.

Show code 
unit_econ = tbls["unit_economics_by_cohort"].copy()
unit_econ["ltv_total"] = unit_econ.ltv_24m * unit_econ.mature_customers
unit_econ["cac_total"] = unit_econ.average_cac * unit_econ.mature_customers
RATIO_RULE = (3.0, 2.0)   # good at or above, watch at or above

def ratio_status(v):
    return "n/a" if pd.isna(v) else "Good" if v >= RATIO_RULE[0] else "Watch" if v >= RATIO_RULE[1] else "Bad"

def sec_ratio(name):
    s, e, _, _ = win_bounds(name)
    u = unit_econ[unit_econ.cohort_month.between(s, e)]
    if u.empty:
        display(Markdown(f"No cohort that signed up in {name} has 24 months of data by 2025-12.")); return
    n = u.cohort_month.nunique()
    overall = u.ltv_total.sum() / u.cac_total.sum()
    badge("LTV:CAC, all customers", f"{n} cohort{'s' if n != 1 else ''}, {u.cohort_month.min()} to {u.cohort_month.max()}", f"{overall:.1f} : 1", ratio_status(overall))
    g2 = u.groupby(["channel", "plan_tier"])[["ltv_total", "cac_total"]].sum()
    ratio = (g2.ltv_total / g2.cac_total).unstack("plan_tier")[SEGMENT_ORDER["plan_tier"]].loc[SEGMENT_ORDER["channel"]]
    txt = ratio.apply(lambda col: col.map(lambda v: f"{v:.1f}  {ratio_status(v)}"))
    css = ratio.apply(lambda col: col.map(lambda v: STATUS_CSS[ratio_status(v)]))
    out = txt.reset_index().rename(columns={"channel": "Channel"})
    cs_ = css.reset_index(drop=True); cs_.insert(0, "Channel", "")
    display(Markdown(f"Based on **{n}** cohort{'s' if n != 1 else ''} that signed up " + (f"from {u.cohort_month.min()} to {u.cohort_month.max()}." if n > 1 else f"in {u.cohort_month.min()}.")))
    display(out.style.hide(axis="index").apply(lambda _: cs_, axis=None))
    lo, hi = ratio.stack().idxmin(), ratio.stack().idxmax()
    display(Markdown(
        ("Every channel and plan tier clears 3 to 1. " if ratio.min().min() >= 3 else "Some groups fall below 3 to 1. ") +
        f"The weakest group is **{lo[0]} {lo[1]}** at **{ratio.stack().min():.1f}**. The strongest is **{hi[0]} {hi[1]}** at **{ratio.stack().max():.1f}**."))
    rt = ratio.reset_index().melt(id_vars="channel", var_name="Plan tier", value_name="ltv_cac")
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(9, 4.8))
    sns.barplot(data=rt, x="channel", y="ltv_cac", hue="Plan tier", order=SEGMENT_ORDER["channel"],
                hue_order=SEGMENT_ORDER["plan_tier"], palette=TIER, ax=ax)
    for c_ in ax.containers: ax.bar_label(c_, fmt="%.1f", fontsize=9, padding=2)
    ax.axhline(3, color="#555555", ls="--", lw=1)
    ax.annotate("3:1 minimum", (1, 3), xycoords=("axes fraction", "data"), xytext=(5, 0), textcoords="offset points",
                va="center", fontsize=9, color="#555555", annotation_clip=False)
    ax.set_xlabel(""); ax.set_ylabel("LTV : CAC"); ax.set_title("LTV:CAC over 24 months"); ax.legend(title="Plan tier", loc="upper left")
    plt.show()

7.2.1 Payback by channel and plan tier

Payback is how many months of revenue it takes to earn back what we paid to win the customer. Fewer months is better. The dashed black line is all customers together. It is exact, and its whole-month value is the figure the old dashboard shows. The colored lines split it by channel and plan tier. Those nine lines are estimates. The export gives each group’s 24-month revenue and CAC, but not its month-by-month revenue. We assume each group earns its revenue on the same schedule as its whole cohort. The ranking of the groups is reliable. The exact month counts are approximate. Adding cumulative LTV by channel and plan tier to the dbt export would make them exact. Only cohorts with 24 months of data by 2025-12 can be split this way, so the last tab has one cohort.

Show code 
cum_ltv_grid = coh_metrics.cumulative_ltv.unstack("period")
PAYBACK_RULE = (6.0, 12.0)   # months. Good at or below the first, Watch at or below the second, otherwise Bad.

def payback_status(v):
    return "n/a" if pd.isna(v) else "Good" if v <= PAYBACK_RULE[0] else "Watch" if v <= PAYBACK_RULE[1] else "Bad"

def payback(cohort):
    l = np.r_[0.0, cum_ltv_grid.loc[cohort].dropna().values]
    c = cac_by_chan.Blended[cohort]
    hit = np.where(l >= c)[0]
    if len(hit) == 0: return np.nan
    m = hit[0]
    return (m - 1) + (c - l[m - 1]) / (l[m] - l[m - 1])
payback_by_coh = pd.Series({k: payback(k) for k in cac_by_chan.index}).dropna()      # all customers, exact

def calc_payback_by_seg():
    """Estimate by channel and plan tier. Each group is assumed to earn its 24-month LTV on its cohort's own schedule."""
    out = []
    for r in unit_econ.itertuples():
        full = cum_ltv_grid.loc[r.cohort_month, list(range(24))].values.astype(float)
        share = np.r_[0.0, full / full[-1]]            # share of 24-month revenue earned after 0, 1, 2 ... months
        need = r.average_cac / r.ltv_24m               # share of 24-month revenue that repays CAC
        hit = np.where(share >= need)[0]
        val = np.nan if len(hit) == 0 else (hit[0] - 1) + (need - share[hit[0] - 1]) / (share[hit[0]] - share[hit[0] - 1])
        out.append((r.cohort_month, r.channel, r.plan_tier, val))
    return pd.DataFrame(out, columns=["cohort_month", "channel", "plan_tier", "months"])
payback_by_seg = calc_payback_by_seg()

def sec_payback_combo(name):
    s, e, _, _ = win_bounds(name)
    cb = payback_by_seg[payback_by_seg.cohort_month.between(s, e)]
    if cb.empty:
        display(Markdown(f"No cohort that signed up in {name} has 24 months of data by 2025-12.")); return
    cs_ = sorted(cb.cohort_month.unique()); n = len(cs_); blended = payback_by_coh.reindex(cs_)
    badge("Average payback, all customers", (f"{n} cohorts, {cs_[0]} to {cs_[-1]}" if n > 1 else f"{cs_[0]} cohort"),
          f"{blended.mean():.1f} months", payback_status(blended.mean()))
    fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 3, figsize=(12.5, 4.3), sharey=True)
    for ax, ch in zip(axes, SEGMENT_ORDER["channel"]):
        for pl in SEGMENT_ORDER["plan_tier"]:
            x_ = cb[(cb.channel == ch) & (cb.plan_tier == pl)].set_index("cohort_month").months
            ax.plot(dt(x_.index), x_.values, color=TIER[pl], lw=2, marker="o" if n < 4 else None, ms=6, label=pl)
        ax.plot(dt(blended.index), blended.values, color=INK, lw=1.2, ls="--", marker="o" if n < 4 else None, ms=4, label="All customers")
        ax.axhline(PAYBACK_RULE[0], color="#999999", lw=0.8, ls=":")
        ax.set_title(ch)
        if n >= 4:
            windowaxis(ax, cs_[0], cs_[-1], months=(1, 7))
        else:
            ax.set_xticks(dt(cs_)); ax.set_xticklabels(cs_); ax.margins(x=0.4)
        ax.tick_params(axis="x", labelsize=8)
    axes[0].set_ylabel("Months to pay back CAC")
    axes[0].set_ylim(0, max(PAYBACK_RULE[0], cb.months.max()) * 1.15)
    axes[2].legend(loc="upper right", fontsize=8)
    fig.suptitle("Estimated months to pay back CAC, by signup cohort (dotted line = 6 months)", x=0.01, ha="left", fontweight="bold", fontsize=12)
    fig.tight_layout(); plt.show()
    rows, css = [], []
    def add(ch_, pl_, x_):
        st = payback_status(x_.mean())
        rows.append({"Channel": ch_, "Plan tier": pl_, "Average (months)": f"{x_.mean():.1f}", "Fastest cohort": f"{x_.min():.1f}",
                     "Slowest cohort": f"{x_.max():.1f}", "Verdict": st})
        css.append({k: "" for k in rows[-1]} | {"Verdict": STATUS_CSS[st]})
    add("All customers", "Blended (exact)", blended)
    for ch in SEGMENT_ORDER["channel"]:
        for pl in SEGMENT_ORDER["plan_tier"]:
            add(ch, pl, cb[(cb.channel == ch) & (cb.plan_tier == pl)].set_index("cohort_month").months)
    display(Markdown(f"Based on **{n}** cohort{'s' if n != 1 else ''}. Good is {PAYBACK_RULE[0]:.0f} months or less, Watch is up to {PAYBACK_RULE[1]:.0f}, Bad is longer. The nine group rows are estimates."))
    display(pd.DataFrame(rows).style.hide(axis="index").apply(lambda _: pd.DataFrame(css), axis=None))
    avg = cb.groupby(["channel", "plan_tier"]).months.mean()
    display(Markdown(f"The fastest group is **{' '.join(avg.idxmin())}** at about **{avg.min():.1f}** months. The slowest is **{' '.join(avg.idxmax())}** at about **{avg.max():.1f}** months."))

9 How each number is calculated

Number Calculation Source tables
ARPU MRR / active customers monthly_metrics_long
ARR 12 x MRR monthly_metrics_long
MoM growth MRR this month / MRR last month - 1 monthly_metrics_long
Logo churn % customers churned / active customers last month monthly_metrics_long
Revenue churn % churn dollars lost / MRR last month mrr_movements_long
Movement share movement dollars / MRR last month mrr_movements_long
NRR (MRR last month + expansion + contraction + churn) / MRR last month mrr_movements_long, nrr_long
Cohort size customers active in month 0 cohort_metrics_long
Retention % customers active / cohort size cohort_metrics_long
Revenue retention % cohort MRR / cohort MRR in month 0 cohort_metrics_long
Revenue per starting customer cohort MRR / cohort size cohort_metrics_long
Cumulative LTV running sum of revenue per starting customer cohort_metrics_long
Blended CAC channel CAC weighted by customers won per channel cac_per_customer_by_channel
LTV:CAC cumulative LTV at month 24 / blended CAC cohort_metrics_long, cac_per_customer_by_channel
LTV:CAC by channel and plan sum of 24-month LTV x mature customers / sum of CAC x mature customers unit_economics_by_cohort
Payback months, all customers first month where cumulative LTV reaches blended CAC, fractional by straight line. The old dashboard shows the whole-month part cohort_metrics_long
Payback months by channel and plan tier (estimate) the share of 24-month revenue that repays CAC (average CAC / 24-month LTV), read off the cohort’s own revenue schedule unit_economics_by_cohort, cohort_metrics_long
Change in a rate latest rate minus earlier rate, in percentage points calculated here
Change in dollars or counts latest / earlier - 1, in percent calculated here
Year-over-year basis December value for MRR, ARR, customers and ARPU. Full-year total for new customers, churned customers and net new MRR. Average month for churn and NRR calculated here
Good / Watch / Bad direction and size rules in RULES, MOVE_RULES, CAC_RULE, RATIO_RULE and PAYBACK_RULE calculated here
Match with the old dashboard every chart’s numbers against saas_dashboard_data.xlsx, when it sits next to the report data checks

Time-series charts (customers, churn, NRR) show the tab’s own months. Cohort charts (retention, CAC, LTV:CAC, payback) show cohorts that signed up in the tab’s window, followed through 2025-12. Segments are all, channel (Ads, Organic, Referral) and plan_tier (Basic, Pro, Enterprise). The report stops at 2025-12 even though the exports run to 2028-12.
